questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: High academic level, English speaking country, and potential outdoor experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great experience all around!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Their website had a lot of information, the student accommodation that you end up at will contact you and send you packing lists etc. Only thing that was never mentioned in time was that the week before the orientation week is an additional and also optional orientation week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a student senior resident at the student accomodation whose job it was to assist us. The international student office at the university was also really helpful and timely.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A lot of different residences are available, and al of them are worth it as an international exchange student as finding housing on your own can be hard.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some residences are catered and prepare food for you, others have kitchens. The kitchen facilities i had at the Yukeembruk residence were really nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
You only get to wish for one of the residences, and if you don't get it you will most likely be placed at the Yukeembruk residence, which is a really nice residence but also one of the most expensive ones.
If i were to choose a residence again i would either choose B&G hall, or Fenner Hall.
Also, most of the social stuff happening on campus and in the orientation week is centered around the residences and not the study programs, so if you don't live on campus you can easily miss out on a lot of social activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register on their registratoin website with a reserved spot (because you are on exchange) and then you sign up for the lectures and lab sesions that fit you in a first-come-first-served basis.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your senior resident, as well as other assigned help you can find at the student services or your residence.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for you exercise sessions asap, the good time slots gets filled up pretty quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lectures were not the quality i expected, but the material and the assignments were really good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A lot of master courses are essentially just bachelor courses you can do as a masters student without it begin much different from taking it as a bachelor student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Here all courses give you a score from 0-100 with total transparency of what points you need to get a certain grade. This also means that all assignments and exams just give you points that counts towards the 100 and everything becomes very quantitative.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational networks in Computing
Analysis 2: Lebesgue Integration and Hilbert Spaces
Statistical Machine Learning
Computer vision

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Computational networks in Computing was a really interesting course that we don't currently have at UCPH.

questions.answer: To apply for a student visa you have to pay a somewhat substantial fee.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Meat is cheaper but greens is more expensive, otherwise it is pretty comparable to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Whole lot of clubs and other activities to do at the university, not that much to do in the city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind of student club you can think of is available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the Caving club if you want to try something really different on your stay abroad.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take weekend trips to the larger cities when not spending it around Canberra.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy, Australia is a really western culture like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get into an on-campus residence, then the rest is easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language was really fun to experience first hand and in a day-to-day setting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember to enjoy other cities than Canberra.
2. Join some student clubs.
3. Go to the big events like Big Night Out that take place on campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that the week just before the orientation week is also an orientation week that focuses on your residences.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience such a great part of the world, both the nature and the people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having time to see it all and do all of the stuff. Australia is such a big and rich country you could spend a lifetime being a tourist there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you go to Australia, definitely go see what the inland areas and the outback are like.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
